diagnostic_targets: Compact relatively short neck compared with long-necked sauropods; robust oval torso and four columnar limbs.
Long narrowing tail ends in modest lobate terminal club, not ankylosaur giant hammer.
Two sequential pairs of small rounded conical dorsal/lateral tail osteoderms per Zhang1988/Remes2009 reconstruction; association in life uncertain, explicitly reconstruction.
Small broad relatively boxy head, closed herbivore jaw, no theropod teeth.
Whole animal includes entire head neck body limbs tail; no skeleton-only or club-only substitute.
uncertainties: Zhang1988 positions small dermal tail spines on T5401 and revised diagnosis mentions two pairs; whether fossils found articulated is not established here. Do not claim in-situ proven location.
Skin colour muscle volume and neutral pose inferred.
Do not copy drooping historical mount pose or modern artwork.
Use modest relative spike size; avoid dramatic Stegosaurus thagomizer.
acceptance_checks: Short neck/body proportion readable in side view.
Four leg-ground contacts, attached transitions, tail not dragging.
Small terminal lobate club and four small spines readable in top/side.
